description: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of mathematical problem types across different educational levels and competition tiers, based on the Odyssey Math dataset. The chart is divided into ten distinct segments, each representing a specific mathematical topic and its associated difficulty level, with labels and percentages provided for each category. The largest segment, colored dark blue, corresponds to Algebra – Olympiad-level, accounting for 21.19% (82 problems). The second largest segment, in light pink, represents Algebra – High School, making up 17.83% (69 problems). Pre-Calculus – High School follows with 14.21% (55 problems), shown in brown. Combinatorics – Olympiad-level contributes 9.56% (37 problems), depicted in light green. Geometry – Olympiad-level accounts for 6.46% (25 problems), shown in orange. Linear Algebra and Abstract Algebra – University-level also represents 6.46% (25 problems), in magenta. Calculus and Analysis – University-level contributes 6.20% (24 problems), in dark gray. Probability – University-level accounts for 5.43% (21 problems), in teal. Differential Equations – University-level represents 3.62% (14 problems), in yellow. Statistics – University-level makes up 4.39% (17 problems), in light blue. Geometry – High School is the smallest segment at 3.62% (14 problems), shown in light purple. The chart includes a legend on the left side, listing the categories with corresponding colors and their respective percentages and problem counts. Each segment is labeled with its full name, percentage, and the number of problems in parentheses, and the percentages are clearly visible within or near each slice. The segments are arranged in a clockwise direction, starting from the top right, with no visual emphasis such as exploded slices.
